profile.headline: Software Engineer II @ Datadog
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
(Cognitive Systems and Research | Observability Graph)
Applying graph databases at scale as part of Representation Primitives, Datadog’s data platform for modeling complex infrastructure relationships to serve learned service observability + reliability insights.

positions.title: Software Engineer III
positions.description:
Moved 1M+ daily requests out of the monolith by migrating class categorization metadata into a Kotlin microservice with Dynamo.

Drove over 60% improved estimated engagement with newly released prerecorded classes by designing and implementing the Premiere feature, a core feature on the Peloton schedule that allows prerecorded classes to be scheduled and joined via livestream. Successfully launched despite high load due to celebrity collaboration (Mariah Carey, Carly Rae Jepsen).

Designed and developed a new microservice-based content management system backend. 

Led development of a Kotlin microservice to manage server-driven UI state of the Peloton homescreen.

Halved latency of several key content endpoints through caching, request batching, SQL query optimization, and reducing network wait.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description: Skills: Kotlin · Python · Back-End Web Development · Microservices · Distributed Systems · REST APIs · gRPC · Git · Amazon Web Services (AWS) · Dynamo · Amazon SQS · EKS · Software Testing · Relational Databases

positions.title: Developer
positions.description:

positions.description:

▪ Developed plotting utility to visualize output and state of life support physics simulations
▪ Tested Orion spacecraft Life Support Systems for NASA crewed missions to the moon with integration and unit tests

projects.title: 1st Prize, USC Makeathon
projects.description:
- Won 1st Place at USC Makeathon: annual, 30-hour hardware hackathon
- Challenge: develop improved walking aid for patients with Parkinson's Disease
- Designed, fabricated, and assembled walker with intuitive, mechanically-activated automatic braking system
- Using Arduino, integrated vibration pads into walker arm guides to serve as tactile cues for patient gait control, with on/off toggle switch
